query: For single-phase ZrB2 ceramic, which requires preparation temperatures above 2300 °C and may lack the strength and structural integrity needed for service, what single intervention could lower the required preparation temperature and reduce the holes and eventual component failure caused by prolonged exposure to a liquid plating bath? State one hypothesis identifying the intervention and its mechanism, predict its performance compared with conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2, define the relevant preparation and service boundaries, identify supporting prior evidence, and describe a controlled preparation, integrity, and long-duration exposure experiment that could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adopting a liquid-phase precursor synthesis combined with spark plasma sintering (SPS) will enable the production of single-phase ZrB2 at temperatures below 2300 °C while simultaneously achieving a denser, more uniform microstructure that reduces porosity and defects responsible for liquid plating bath-induced damage.
generation.material_initial_state: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 produced via high-temperature (>2300 °C) solid-state sintering, characterized by inherent porosity and microstructural imperfections.
generation.intervention: Use a liquid-phase precursor method to prepare nanoscale ZrB2 particles combined with rapid consolidation via spark plasma sintering.
generation.conditions: Preparation conducted at significantly lower temperatures (targeting approximately 1800–2000 °C) followed by long-duration exposure testing in a liquid plating bath environment.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced densification and uniform grain structure due to the rapid sintering of nanoscale powders, leading to reduced pore and defect formation.
generation.mechanism: The liquid-phase precursor yields fine, uniform ZrB2 powders that sinter rapidly under SPS, promoting a homogeneous microstructure with lower porosity. This improved microstructural integrity enhances resistance to the chemical/mechanical degradation induced by prolonged liquid plating exposure.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared with conventional high-temperature sintered ZrB2, the proposed method is expected to reduce the required sintering temperature and produce a ceramic with fewer pores and holes, thereby improving mechanical strength and service life under liquid plating conditions.
generation.baseline: Conventionally processed ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C that exhibits significant porosity and structural imperfections, leading to lower durability during long-term liquid exposure.
generation.boundary: Preparation boundary: conventional temperatures >2300 °C versus targeted processing temperatures of 1800–2000 °C; Service boundary: extended exposure to a liquid plating bath where conventional materials exhibit pore formation and eventual failure.
generation.uncertainty: The precise reduction in sintering temperature and the quantitative improvement in mechanical integrity remain to be experimentally determined. Additionally, ensuring phase purity and reproducibility in nano-precursor processing is an area of potential variability.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of single-phase ZrB2 samples: one set using conventional high-temperature (above 2300 °C) sintering, and another set using the liquid-phase precursor method combined with SPS at 1800–2000 °C. Characterize both sets for phase purity (using XRD), microstructural features (using SEM), and porosity. Subsequently, subject the samples to a simulated liquid plating bath for an extended duration (e.g., 100–200 hours) under controlled conditions.
measurements: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) to quantify grain size and porosity
Mechanical testing (e.g., microhardness and flexural strength) before and after liquid bath exposure
Long-term durability assessments by monitoring the development of pores or cracks
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the samples produced using the liquid-phase precursor and SPS method do not show a statistically significant reduction in porosity and an improvement in mechanical integrity after liquid exposure compared to the conventionally sintered samples, the hypothesis is falsified.

Here, we aim to produce single-phase high-entropy oxides composed of Co-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ni-O through spark plasma sintering (SPS), testing their thermoelectric (TE) properties. This material was successfully obtained before via a different technique, which requires a very long processing time. Hence, the main target of this work is to apply spark plasma sintering, a much faster and scalable process. The samples were sintered in the temperature range of 1200–1300 °C. Two main phases were formed: rock salt-structured Fm3̅m and spinel-structured Fd3̅m. Comparable transport properties were achieved via the new approach: the highest value of the Seebeck coefficient reached −112.6 μV/K at room temperature, compared to −150 μV/K reported before; electrical properties at high temperatures are close to the properties of the single-phase material (σ = 0.2148 S/cm, σ ≈ 0.2009 S/cm reported before). These results indicate that SPS can be successfully applied to produce highly efficient TE high-entropy alloys in a fast and scalable way. Further optimization

AbstractA nano-dual-phase powder with ultra-fine grain size was synthesized by the liquid precursor method at 1200 °C. A series of single-phase high-entropy ceramic powders ((Ti, Zr, Hf, Nb)B2, (Ti, Zr, Hf, Nb, Ta)B2, (Ti, Zr, Hf, Nb, Mo)B2, (Ti, Zr, Hf, Nb, Ta, Mo)B2) with high purity (C content less than 0.9 wt% and O content less than 0.7 wt%) and ultrafine (average grain sizes of 340–570 nm) were successfully synthesized at 1800 °C. The sample of (TiZrHfNbTa)B2 exhibited a hexagonal close-packed (HCP) structure, and the metal elements were uniformly distributed at the nanoscale, microscale, and macroscale. This method did not apply to the preparation of all high-entropy ceramic powders and was unfavorable for the formation of single-phase high-entropy borides when the size difference factor exceeded 3.9%. The present work provides a guide for the development of ceramic-based composites through precursor impregnation pyrolysis.Keywords: liquid-phase precursor method, high-entropy diboride powders, solid solutions, microstructure, pyrolysis mechanism

The equiatomic Ti-V-Nb-Ta alloy is one of the most attractive RHEAs, which solidifies as a single-phase body-centered cubic (BCC) microstructure with heterogeneous elemental distribution and exhibits excellent high-temperature strength and room-temperature ductility (). Equimolar Ti-V-Nb-Ta has an extremely high compressive yield strength, 1273 MPa at room temperature and 688 MPa at 900°C (). By comparison, conventional high-temperature Ni-base superalloys notably soften above 600°C, with the compressive yield strength dropping to ~200 MPa at 900°C (). Equimolar Ti-V-Nb-Ta also exhibits impressive tensile ductility, ~14% at room temperature (), and a relatively low brittle-to-ductile transition temperature between −47° and −27°C, comparable to BCC metals and stainless steels for engineering applications (, ). In this study, a novel three-phase BCC + B2 + FCC AlCoFeNi MEA was designed and manufactured using the SLM method. The microstructure evolution and mechanical properties before and after heat treatment were investigated. The key findings are summarized as follows: SLM can be used to fabricate an AlCoFeNi MEA, which shows good performance. The as-built samples exhibit a single BCC phase consisting of columnar and equiaxed grains, which achieved a high density of 99.97%, a hardness of 32.5 HRC, a YS of 1023.1 MPa, a UTS of 1211.5 MPa, and an El of 10.8%. Phase transformation occurred during the aging treatment, and a complex three-phase structure comprising BCC, B2, and FCC phases was achieved. With an increase in aging temperature and duration, an evident reduction in the content of the BCC/B2 phases was detected, accompanied by an increase in the FCC phases. It is obvious that the influence of the aging temperature on phase transformation is more significant than the aging time. The MEA achieved a well-balanced combination of hardness, strength, and toughness after the heat treatment. decision.trend: Early work on high-temperature ceramics like ZrB2 has relied on conventional sintering at temperatures above 2300 °C, which often produces materials with inherent porosity and microstructural flaws that reduce service integrity. More recent studies in related ceramic systems and high‐entropy ceramic powders have shifted toward alternative processing routes such as the liquid-phase precursor method (as in PMC10707663) and spark plasma sintering (as in PMC10134248) to achieve rapid densification at lower temperatures. These approaches use nanoscale precursor powders and rapid consolidation techniques to enhance microstructural uniformity and lower processing temperatures; however, they have mostly been applied to multi-principal (high-entropy) compounds rather than the single-phase ZrB2 system.
decision.unsolved: For single-phase ZrB2 ceramics, there remains an unmet need for a single intervention that both reduces the high sintering temperature requirement and simultaneously improves the microstructural integrity (minimizing the formation of pores and holes during long-term liquid exposure) without sacrificing phase purity.
decision.lever: Adopt a liquid-phase precursor synthesis combined with rapid consolidation techniques (such as spark plasma sintering) to produce nanoscale, high-purity single-phase ZrB2 powders at a significantly lowered temperature (<2300 °C)
decision.why: This approach follows the trend identified in ceramic processing research where alternative synthesis routes enable lower temperature densification and improved microstructure. The use of a liquid-phase precursor can yield nanoscale powders that sinter quickly and uniformly under SPS, thereby reducing processing temperature and minimizing porosity. This single, unified intervention addresses both the preparation and service defects (i.e., liquid bath induced microstructural damage) highlighted in the research question.
